item.title: Submit Duty Conditions
item.description:
Why duty conditions matter

Most selection delays begin with missing operating information. A valve name alone is not enough for corrosive or chemical service because body material, seat material, elastomer, actuator size, end connection, pressure class, and document package all depend on the actual duty.

Clear duty conditions help the first response move from broad guessing to useful clarification: which product families fit, which assumptions are risky, which documents are needed, and which items require customer or engineering confirmation.

item.title: Material Compatibility Review
item.description:
What compatibility review covers

Material compatibility is a structured review, not a single yes-or-no answer. The same chemical can behave differently depending on concentration, temperature, pressure, aeration, contaminants, exposure time, intermittent drying, and cleaning practice.

For flow control products, the weak point is not always the valve body. Seats, seals, diaphragms, liners, gaskets, fasteners, tubing, adapters, and instrument accessories may all need attention.

Typical questions

Question Why it matters
What is the exact media and concentration? A broad chemical family can include very different corrosion behavior.
What is the temperature range? Compatibility may change sharply at elevated temperature or during cleaning.
Is the service oxidizing, abrasive, crystallizing, or solvent-based? The risk may shift from body corrosion to seat, seal, diaphragm, or wear issues.
Is exposure continuous or intermittent? Drying, crystallization, flushing, and startup conditions can affect the recommendation.
Are there outdoor or corrosive atmosphere conditions? External fasteners, actuator housings, coatings, and accessories may need review.

What Nuvon can provide

Nuvon can organize a material direction, a shortlist of product families, missing information, and points requiring customer or engineering confirmation. Where uncertainty remains, the quotation should state assumptions clearly instead of implying that a final engineering approval has already been completed.

item.title: Submittal & Documentation
item.description:
Why documentation belongs in the scope

For many international projects, the document package is part of the product. A valve can be physically correct but still delay approval if datasheets, drawings, material declarations, test records, or packing documents are missing or inconsistent.

Nuvon treats documentation as a scope item that should be discussed during RFQ preparation, not as an afterthought once goods are ready to ship.

Common submittal items

Document type Typical use
Technical datasheet Confirms product family, size, material, connection, pressure class, and accessory scope.
General arrangement or dimensional drawing Supports layout, pipe connection, installation clearance, and drawing review.
IOM manual Helps project teams check installation, operation, maintenance, and storage expectations.
Material or compliance declaration Supports customer review where material traceability or compliance statements are required.
Inspection or test record May be requested for pressure tests, functional checks, or project quality review.
Packing and marking documents Helps coordinate shipment, labeling, spare parts, and receiving inspection.

Document control notes

If a project uses a document register, tag list, revision table, file naming rule, language requirement, or approval status workflow, include those requirements at the RFQ stage. Document revisions should be traceable so that quotation scope, production confirmation, and shipment documents do not drift apart.

item.title: RFQ & BOM Support
item.description:
RFQ and BOM challenges

Many project requests start as screenshots, partial line lists, mixed valve names, pipe sizes, or copied BOM rows. That is normal, but it can create hidden assumptions: one line may be missing material, another may omit end connection, and another may require an actuator or document package that is not visible.

Nuvon can help organize the request so both sides can see what is being quoted, what is assumed, and what still needs confirmation.
